name: Invisible text instruction
description: Instructions hidden using CSS to make text invisible to humans but readable by agents. The hiding styles display none, visibility hidden and white text on a white background are flagged where they appear in the forms the tests cover, with one structural tag-name exception: a start tag whose name, spelled in ASCII letters, is an image, input, meta, source, track, embed, line break or rule tag, or a frame or a script tag closed at once, followed by whitespace, a slash or the end of the tag. Tags of that kind hold no text of their own in an HTML document, so an input that holds an svg or math start tag gets no exception at all, because the same names can hold text in that content. A name that only starts like one of these, or that uses a non ASCII letter that folds onto an ASCII one, is another element and is flagged, and so is a link tag. The attribute text on the excepted tags is not read, except that a frame with a srcdoc is flagged. A hidden element outside the exception is flagged, including hidden interface text such as a closed cookie dialog.
